title: Build a business case
summary: A business case shows why an investment is worth making: the problem, the options, the costs, the benefits and the risks. It helps leaders decide and gives you a baseline to measure against.

beginner: State the problem and why it matters now.
List the options, including doing nothing.
For each, estimate costs: people, tools, running costs.
Estimate benefits: money, time saved, risk reduced, user value.
List the main risks and assumptions.
Recommend an option and say how you will measure success.
intermediate: Estimate costs and benefits with ranges.
Recommend an option with success measures.
experienced: Model sensitivity to the biggest assumptions.
Stage investment so later money depends on early evidence.
Write it so a senior reader can decide in ten minutes.

toolExamples.google-docs: Write the narrative with a short options table.
toolExamples.sharepoint-word: Use your organisation's template if there is one.
toolExamples.claude: Ask it to check your arithmetic and find missing costs.

definitionOfDone: Costs and benefits estimated with ranges
